intro: Environmental engineers solve complex problems with water, soil and air, skills used in planning, science and resource management. The closest of the 25 careers below is Water Resource Specialists, with a 93% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $167,220 for its broader group, well above the $107,110 environmental engineers earn.
why_it_works: Your work means testing sites, designing treatment systems and coordinating with regulators, contractors and communities. O*NET rates complex problem solving and judgment at 3.88 out of 5 for this job and coordination at 3.75. Water resources, brownfield redevelopment and hydrology use the same expertise. Most matches need no new degree. The gaps are equipment selection, programming and quality checks.
tips: Brownfield redevelopment is an 89% match and uses your site cleanup knowledge.
Materials Scientists earn $117,790, which is 10% more, and are an 80% match.
Information Security Analysts earn $129,180, or 21% more, if you move toward data and systems.

faq.q: What jobs can former environmental engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Water Resource Specialists (93%), brownfield redevelopment specialists (89%) and Hydrologists (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Hydrologists earn $96,600, which is 10% less than the $107,110 environmental engineer median, and focus more on research.

faq.q: Which careers for environmental engineers pay more?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more. Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 (38% more), Database Architects $139,500 (30% more) and Information Security Analysts $129,180 (21% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Water Resource Specialists earn $167,220 for their broader group.

faq.q: Do environmental engineers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than environmental engineers already have, including all of the top 10, while 3 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 77% of workers in a close match.

faq.q: What skills should environmental engineers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment selection, programming, quality control analysis and troubleshooting. Time management already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so technical and software skills are the main steps for most moves.
